default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1428.title: Clock-hour anchored VWAP reclaim
E-1428.hypothesis: Desks that work orders by the clock hour benchmark the VWAP that restarts at each hour; after the price sat on one side of that hour's VWAP for a while, the first close back across it puts the hour's participants on the other side of their average cost, and their covering plus new entries push on.

E-1429.title: Frozen first-window VWAP cross
E-1429.hypothesis: The VWAP of the opening 30-90 minutes freezes into the average cost of the opening institutions' inventory; unlike the running session VWAP it no longer moves, so a first close back across it after a dwell flips that cohort between profit and loss and they defend or abandon it together; follow the cross.

E-1430.title: Whole-run erase bar
E-1430.hypothesis: After a run of same-colour bars, a single bar that closes beyond the OPEN of the first bar of the run has erased the whole run in one auction: everyone who traded the run is under water at once and their exits join the new side; follow the erasing bar.

E-1431.title: Short clock-block open reclaim
E-1431.hypothesis: Chart traders and bots mark the open of every 10/15/30-minute candle; after price stayed on one side of the current candle's open for part of the candle, a close back across flips the candle's colour, triggering the stops and reversals of those positioned for the old colour; follow the flip.

E-1432.title: Swing-count rotation fade
E-1432.hypothesis: A session whose price has already completed several full swings of a fixed size (counted with a zigzag) is a rotational auction where both edges are defended; a short-term break of the 15-minute box in such a day is one more swing end that liquidity providers lean against, so fade it.

E-1433.title: Three-inside confirmation
E-1433.hypothesis: A large bar, a smaller opposite bar inside its body (the push stalls), and a third bar that closes beyond the first bar's open shows the first bar's aggressors were fully absorbed and the other side took the whole range back; follow the confirming bar.

E-1434.title: Equal-close stick sandwich
E-1434.hypothesis: Two same-colour bars closing at the same price with an opposite bar between them mean a resting order stopped the price at that level twice; sellers (buyers) pushed back to the same close and could not go through, so trade away from the level.

E-1435.title: VWAP hold confirmed by the other market's side
E-1435.hypothesis: WIN and WDO move inversely when foreign flow drives both; a touch of VWAP that closes back on the trend side is a stronger hold when the other market sits on the opposite side of its own session average, because the macro flow agrees with the dip being bought (sold).

E-1436.title: Nested clock-open alignment
E-1436.hypothesis: When the price is beyond the open of the current fast clock candle and of the current slow clock candle by a margin, every horizon of candle-reading desks sees the same colour and nobody is on the right side of both; follow the first bar where the alignment appears.

E-1437.title: Exit-scale point thrust
E-1437.hypothesis: A single bar that travels a fixed absolute number of index points (a size comparable to the trade scale, whatever the volatility regime) and closes in the top/bottom third is a stop cascade or parent-order burst that has not met resistance; follow it.
